subtheme: Making sure AI systems do what we actually want

subsubthemes.name: Learning what humans actually prefer
subsubthemes.gist: Training AI systems to match human preferences by collecting feedback on model outputs and adjusting the system to produce what people actually want.

subsubthemes.name: Catching systems that game the rules or lie
subsubthemes.gist: Detecting when AI systems manipulate their outputs to appear aligned while hiding problematic behavior, reward hacking, or providing false information.

subsubthemes.name: Defending against attacks and adversarial tricks
subsubthemes.gist: Building AI systems that stay safe and useful when someone actively tries to manipulate or break them.

subsubthemes.name: Balancing safety without making systems useless
subsubthemes.gist: Finding the right tradeoff between preventing harm and keeping AI systems helpful and capable for real tasks.

subsubthemes.name: Handling disagreement and fairness across groups
subsubthemes.gist: Managing situations where different people want different things, and making sure AI systems work fairly for everyone regardless of background.

subsubthemes.name: Steering what's inside the model
subsubthemes.gist: Using fine-grained control of model internals—activation patterns, reasoning steps, causal pathways—to shape behavior without retraining the whole system.
